rule: Single arrow rotates 90° clockwise per step along each row (row 3: down, left, up); columns rotate 90° counter-clockwise; main diagonal is all 'up'.
T rotates 45° clockwise per step along rows (stem E→SE→S; SE→S→SW; NE→E→SE); columns go +45 then -90, same result: stem pointing SE.
Count is a distribution of three {1,2,3} per row/column (row 3: 3,2,1); direction rotates 90° clockwise per step along rows (row 3: NE, SE, SW). Answer: 1 arrow pointing SW.
Dot sits on an 8-spot ring (corners + edge midpoints) and moves 90° clockwise per step along rows (BR→BL→TL; L→T→R; R→B→L). Columns (+135°, then +180°) agree.
legibility: Corner and edge-midpoint dot positions sit on the same small ring (e.g. BR in cell 1 vs R in cell 7). At ~38 dp per square that is only a few dp of difference, so they can be confused at a glance.

rule: Dot in circle moves 90° counter-clockwise across the 4 diagonal spots per step along rows (row 3: BL, BR, TR); columns (ccw, then 180°) agree.
Distribution of three for both attributes: outer frame {square, hexagon, circle} and inner symbol {triangle, cross, star}. Row 3 lacks hexagon + triangle.
shortcut: only novel option: options 1 (=cell 2), 2 (=cell 7) and 4 (=cell 5) copy matrix cells, so the answer is the only combination not already shown

rule: Line segments (4 square edges + 2 diagonals): cell3 = cell1 XOR cell2 along rows. Rows 1 and 2 rule out union. Row 3: {\,/,B} XOR {L,B,/} = {L,\}.
shortcut: none (every option has 2 segments; each segment appears in exactly 2 options)
legibility: Thin strokes (~2 dp at phone size); edges and diagonals overlap at the corners. Still readable.

rule: Line segments: cell3 = cell1 UNION cell2 along rows (shared segments are kept, which rules out XOR). Row 3: {T,L,/} ∪ {T,L,B} = {T,L,B,/}.
shortcut: none (all options have 4 segments; the features are spread symmetrically)

rule: Dots on 5 spots (4 corners + centre): cell3 = cell1 XOR cell2 along rows (row 1 rules out union). Row 3: {TL,C,BL,BR} XOR {TR,BL,BR} = {TL,TR,C}.
shortcut: none (all options have 3 dots; spot features are spread cyclically)

rule: Dots in circle: cell3 = cell1 UNION cell2 along rows (row 1 keeps the shared TR, which rules out XOR). Row 3: {C,BL} ∪ {TR,C} = {BL,C,TR}.
Count +1 per step along rows (row 3: 2,3,4); shape is a distribution of three {circle, square, diamond} in each row/column. Answer: 4 circles.

Fill is a distribution of three {outline, dotted, solid}. Count: in each row the first two cells are equal and the third is one fewer (4,4,3); columns also go +1 per row (1,2,3 in col 3). Answer: 3 dotted triangles.
shortcut: none (the answer is identical to cell 4, so an 'avoid copies' heuristic would actually mislead)
legibility: Dotted triangles are small: ~19 dp triangle with a ~5 dp dot, 4 per cell. Readable but tight.

rule: Distribution of three for shape {hexagon, square, diamond} and fill {hatched, outline, solid}. Row 3 lacks a hatched square.
shortcut: only novel option: options 1 (=cell 4), 2 (=cell 1) and 4 (=cell 8) copy matrix cells
legibility: Hatch has rendering artifacts: thick black wedges where hatch lines meet the outline at corners (cells 1 and 5). Hatch spacing is ~3 dp on a phone and reads as grey; still distinct from solid and outline.

rule: Direction is constant within each row (SE / SW / NW); count +1 per step along rows (row 3: 1,2,3). Columns repeat the 1,2,1 / 2,3,2 / 3,4,3 pattern. Answer: 3 arrows pointing NW.
Fill is a distribution of three {solid, outline, dotted}; count +1 per step along rows (row 3: 2,3,4). Answer: 4 outline circles.
Distribution of three for shape {diamond, square, triangle} and fill {dotted, outline, solid}; count fixed at 2. Row 3 lacks outline diamonds.
shortcut: only novel option: options 1 (=cell 5), 3 (=cell 3) and 4 (=cell 4) copy matrix cells
legibility: ok (dotted diamonds are small but readable)

rule: Fill is a distribution of three {hatched, solid, outline}; arrow rotates 90° clockwise per step along rows (row 3: SE, SW, NW). Answer: hatched arrow pointing NW.
legibility: Hatch is drawn at one fixed 45° angle, so on NE/SW arrows it runs parallel to the shaft and looks like 1–2 inner stripes (cell 5, option 3), while on N/S/NW arrows it crosses the shaft (cell 1, option 1). 'Hatched' therefore looks different by orientation. Lines are ~1 dp in the matrix, which risks confusion with outline.

rule: Frame is a distribution of three {circle, hexagon, square}; arrow rotates 90° clockwise per step along rows (row 3: E, S, W). Answer: circle with a left arrow.
Frame is a distribution of three {hexagon, square, circle}; dots: cell3 = cell1 XOR cell2 along rows (row 2 rules out simple subtraction). Row 3: {C,BL} XOR {TR,C,BL,BR} = {TR,BR} in a square.
Frame is a distribution of three {circle, square, diamond}; dot moves 90° clockwise around the 4 edge spots per step along rows (B→L→T; T→R→B; L→T→R). Answer: circle with the dot on the right.
shortcut: none (the answer is identical to cell 5, so an 'avoid copies' heuristic would mislead)

rule: Count +1 per step along rows (row 3: 1,2,3); direction rotates 90° counter-clockwise per step along rows (NE→NW→SW; W→S→E; E→N→W). Answer: 3 arrows pointing W.

Shape {arrow, pie, T} and fill {hatched, solid, outline} are each a distribution of three, so the answer is a solid arrow (options 2/4). Orientation: every shape rotates 90° clockwise per step along rows when read from its natural upright (arrow up, pie notch up, letter T upright; equivalently T read by its crossbar side). Row 1: W, N, E; row 2: NE, SE, SW; row 3: SW, NW, NE. Solving for unknown per-shape offsets with a constant row step forces this uniquely.
shortcut: none (options 1/3 are hatched T's, ruled out by shape and fill; the choice between NE and SE needs the rotation rule; option 4 is cell 5's arrow with its fill swapped)
legibility: Three different shapes at ~29 dp. The orientation cue of the pie (a 90° notch) and of the T (crossbar side vs stem) is small. The hatch angle is fixed, so stripes run along the T crossbar but across the stem (cell 8, options 1/3). If a solver reads T by its stem, rows look inconsistent: the crux is non-obvious, not ambiguous.

rule: Frame is a distribution of three {hexagon, circle, square}; dots: cell3 = cell1 UNION cell2 along rows (the shared dot is kept, which rules out XOR). Row 3: {TR,BL} ∪ {C,BL} = {TR,C,BL} in a circle.
Fill is a distribution of three {solid, outline, hatched}; T rotates 45° clockwise per step along rows (stem W→NW→N; SE→S→SW; E→SE→S). Answer: outline upright T (stem down).
